frames.narration: Merge sort on 1,000 numbers: split the list in half, sort each half the same way, merge the two sorted halves. The recursion goes 11 levels deep, until the pieces are single elements.

Add up the recursion tree. Every level merges all 1,000 elements once, so each level costs about the same, and there are about log2 n levels. In total 8,741 comparisons and 9,976 copies: 18,717 operations, about two per element per level. That is n log n growth.

The master theorem is a comparison of levels. For T(n) = a T(n/b) + f(n), either the leaves cost the most (tree sum: 2,047 for 1,024 elements), or the root does (a combine costing n squared: 2,096,128 in total, half of it at the root), or every level ties (merge sort: 11,264). Find the dominant level and you have the total.
Uneven splits. Cut 25% and 75% and the pieces still shrink by a constant factor: 25 levels, 23,121 operations. Cut 10% and 90%: 59 levels, 38,125 operations. Still n log n, with a bigger constant.

Peel off one element at a time and it is no longer dividing anything: 1,000 levels, 757,941 operations, and a stack frame per element. That is worse than insertion sort, which needs 513,893. A quicksort with a consistently bad pivot degrades the same way.

More sub-problems cost more than they look. Eight half-sized sub-problems with an n-squared combine (block matrix multiply) cost 2,146,435,072 at n = 1,024. Seven, as in Strassen's rearrangement, cost 657,710,813. One fewer sub-problem changes the exponent, not just a constant.

The halves are independent, so give them to workers. But for 2 to the power 20 elements the work is 22,020,096 while the span, the chain of steps that must run in order, is 2,097,151, because the last merge touches every element alone. Parallelism is only about 10: 16 or 64 workers take the same time.

Make the merge parallel too and the span falls to about 2,871 in this model, so thousands of workers become useful. In practice also stop recursing below a size threshold and use a simple method on small pieces: the call and task overhead is not free.
